w.e: Anglo F., a hearing, from OF. oïr, F. ouïr, to hear, L. audire. See Audible.

d: Hear; attend; -- a term used by criers of courts to secure silence before making a proclamation. It is repeated three times. [Written also oyes.]
w.e: Anglo-F. oyez hear ye. See Oyer.

d: 2. A name popularly given to the delicate morsel contained in a small cavity of the bone on each side of the lower part of the back of a fowl. Fresh-water oyster (Zoöl.), any species of the genus Etheria, and allied genera, found in rivers of Africa and South America.
